I had my wisdom teeth pulled a year ago and over the course of weeks and months I found it fascinating watching these giant gashed wounds in my mouth slowly heal over and return to a normal state. I found it really interesting how the body has all these self mechanized drills to perform to heal up whatever's thrown at it.

Having teeth yanked from your jaw is a pretty unnatural injury, yet the body still knows really well how to recover and heal from such trauma as if it's been automated and programmed to be prepared for any imaginable wound. Sure to a layman it's just 'oh ya whatever, blood clotting yada yada' but when you learn about microbiology and how your entire body's basically made up of miniature microscopic molecular machines, almost like specialized biological robots it's really kind of mind mindbogglingly amazing.

It's like our body's are aware of itself beyond a whole different level, as if our body's themselves are more intelligent than us ourselves. For how insanely complex our body's are, for it to be pre-equipped with the ability to repair itself completely on it's own without any conscious intervention is really cool.
Anyone else think it's pretty crazy how the body knows to repair itself?

Just imagine what your skin would look like if you couldn't heal past the scarring phase.

Also, our medicine largely relies on our ability to self-repair. Surgery for example would be impossible without our ability to bind incisions back together, blood vessels, etc.. Most doctor techniques are cutting and sewing us up like garments, when you think about it.

Medicine is a poorly understood field as well. If we had a better handle on it, then our pills and such wouldn't have side effects. The reason they do is we don't know how to tune a compound well enough not to have some kind of collateral damage/effect on the body.
